governance.constitution:
- Organize Refine as Foundation, Capabilities, and Surfaces. Foundation holds the durable concepts, Capabilities own the powers and product semantics, and Surfaces remain replaceable adapters.
- Keep the foundation small and legible: Nodes, Goals, Features, target-app context, workflow state, settings, and evidence must remain explicit enough for people and agents to inspect.
- Keep Process, Agents, and Workflow as shared capabilities. They may evolve or be replaced, but their responsibilities and composition must remain coherent across the system.
- Preserve local ownership. Authoritative state, Git history, settings, runtime records, and agent output must be inspectable and recoverable; caches and projections must remain derived.
- Be agent-first by using installed coding-agent CLIs and host tools through shared configuration, process supervision, workflow, and evidence rather than provider- or surface-specific product paths.
- Treat workflow as durable state advancement, process as the observable execution substrate, and agents as actors that use both without redefining either.
- Prefer mitigation and accountability over broad capability denial: isolation, Git, governance, quality, review, visible errors, and recovery should make powerful work safe enough to use.
- Preserve room for architectural discovery. A better design may replace current machinery when it explains the tradeoff, protects product intent, and supplies proportionate migration and verification evidence.
governance.product: Refine is a local-first, agent-first operating layer for software delivery. It turns understandable Goals and Features into reviewable changes by coordinating explicit workflow state, supervised processes, installed coding-agent CLIs, Git isolation, quality, governance, and durable evidence across one or many Nodes. Its core promise is that powerful autonomous work remains user-owned, inspectable, recoverable, and consistent across replaceable human and agent surfaces.

rules.text: Respect the Foundation-Capabilities-Surfaces boundary: durable concepts belong in the model and target-app foundation, product behavior and orchestration belong in shared capabilities, and UI, CLI, API, desktop, and agent surfaces stay thin and semantically consistent.

Compose the existing Process, Agents, Workflow, Git, state, quality, governance, and evidence capabilities before creating new machinery. Each concern should have one authoritative implementation and source of truth unless the Goal explicitly proposes an architectural replacement.

Keep the daemon and surfaces responsive by running agent, Git, quality, lifecycle, and other long-running work through the supervised process substrate with explicit ownership, status, logs, cancellation, failure feedback, and recovery.

Coordinate parallel or distributed work explicitly through Node ownership, workflow claims and capacity, dependency or Feature ordering, and isolated Git branches or worktrees so concurrent changes remain reviewable and recoverable.

Require evidence proportional to actual architectural and operational risk. Verify the affected behavior with the smallest focused checks that provide confidence, including integration or failure-path evidence when a change alters concurrency, persistence, process, Git, release, recovery, or cross-surface semantics. Update only affected docs/intent pages when documented product intent or an architectural contract changes; do not require unrelated documentation or broad cleanup.

Correct the production split-brain in Refine runtime and binary path ownership.

Desired invariant:
- A Refine checkout is the sole product home for its executable and runtime artifacts in every supported launch mode.
- Whether operators run ./r system start, ./r system install --port 8082 followed by service-manager lifecycle, the checkout-local deployed binary directly, or source-promotion/update flows, all normal production runtime files for a port resolve to the same canonical <refine-checkout>/run/<port> tree.
- The stable deployed binary remains <refine-checkout>/bin/refine and installed service definitions execute that checkout-local binary. Do not copy or relocate the Refine binary into ~/.local, XDG application-state directories, or another user-global install location.
- OS-required registration files may remain in their platform-required locations, such as the systemd user-unit or launchd plist directory, but they must reference the checkout-local binary, use the Refine checkout as the working directory, and pass the absolute checkout-local runtime root.

Observed evidence in current main:
- src/surfaces/cli/actions/system.rs defaults --runtime-root to the relative path run, and src/surfaces/cli/dispatch.rs resolves relative CLI paths from the current working directory. Direct binary use outside the checkout can therefore create or consult a second run tree.
- src/process/supervisor/runtime/mod.rs exposes RuntimeRoot::installed_user and RuntimePathLayout::for_os, which models Linux installed runtime state at ${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/refine/run and analogous non-checkout roots on other platforms.
- src/tools/host/installation/backend_spec.rs consumes that OS-specific layout for installed-service metadata, preserving the incorrect alternative product-home concept.
- scripts/install.sh and r already intend the deployed executable to be <checkout>/bin/refine; preserve and strengthen this behavior.
- The live development instance on port 8082 currently reports /home/buddy/projects/refine/run/8082, demonstrating the intended directory shape.

Implementation constraints:
- Establish one shared, explicit checkout discovery/path-resolution capability rather than fixing individual commands independently. Anchor the product default runtime root to the canonical Refine checkout, not process CWD, HOME, XDG_STATE_HOME, install mode, or service-manager mode.
- Route CLI lifecycle commands, installed-service generation and repair, daemon handoffs, deployed update/source promotion, web/Desktop lifecycle surfaces, and installer/runbook paths through the same invariant. Preserve port scoping and multi-checkout isolation.
- Remove or retire production use of RuntimeRoot::installed_user and OS-specific app-support runtime-root selection. Keep separately required credential stores and service-registration locations platform appropriate.
- Preserve explicit injectable runtime roots where test harnesses or deliberately isolated internal execution require them, but normal user-facing start/install/update/repair/status flows must not silently select an external or caller-CWD run directory.
- Detect legacy external runtime/install state safely. Do not silently merge, delete, or overwrite either tree. Provide clear diagnostics and an auditable, non-destructive migration or repair path if existing installed services point outside the checkout.
- Preserve confirmation boundaries for update, uninstall, source promotion, approval, and merge. Do not approve or merge this Goal.
- Update intent and specification, CLI reference, install and upgrade runbooks, and ontology statements that currently permit user-global runtime roots.

Verification:
- Add regression tests proving system start and system install for the same checkout and port resolve byte-for-byte to <checkout>/run/<port>, including invocation from a different CWD and direct use of <checkout>/bin/refine.
- Assert generated systemd, launchd, and service metadata uses the checkout-local binary, checkout working directory, and absolute checkout-local runtime root; assert no production path is ~/.local, XDG state, or another external app-support runtime.
- Cover install, repair, start, stop, restart, status, update, source-promotion handoff, and non-destructive legacy detection at focused shared boundaries.
- Run focused runtime, installation, daemon-lifecycle, CLI, deployed-update, and source-promotion tests; production binary install and install-uninstall coverage; cargo check --all-targets; cargo fmt --all -- --check; documentation contract tests; and git diff --check. Report any unrelated baseline failure or unavailable environment-dependent test separately.

Correct the production split-brain in Refine runtime and binary path ownership.

Desired invariant:
- A Refine checkout is the sole product home for its executable and runtime artifacts in every supported launch mode.
- Whether operators run ./r system start, ./r system install --port 8082 followed by service-manager lifecycle, the checkout-local deployed binary directly, or source-promotion/update flows, all normal production runtime files for a port resolve to the same canonical <refine-checkout>/run/<port> tree.
- The stable deployed binary remains <refine-checkout>/bin/refine and installed service definitions execute that checkout-local binary. Do not copy or relocate the Refine binary into ~/.local, XDG application-state directories, or another user-global install location.
- OS-required registration files may remain in their platform-required locations, such as the systemd user-unit or launchd plist directory, but they must reference the checkout-local binary, use the Refine checkout as the working directory, and pass the absolute checkout-local runtime root.

Observed evidence in current main:
- src/surfaces/cli/actions/system.rs defaults --runtime-root to the relative path run, and src/surfaces/cli/dispatch.rs resolves relative CLI paths from the current working directory. Direct binary use outside the checkout can therefore create or consult a second run tree.
- src/process/supervisor/runtime/mod.rs exposes RuntimeRoot::installed_user and RuntimePathLayout::for_os, which models Linux installed runtime state at ${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/refine/run and analogous non-checkout roots on other platforms.
- src/tools/host/installation/backend_spec.rs consumes that OS-specific layout for installed-service metadata, preserving the incorrect alternative product-home concept.
- scripts/install.sh and r already intend the deployed executable to be <checkout>/bin/refine; preserve and strengthen this behavior.
- The live development instance on port 8082 currently reports /home/buddy/projects/refine/run/8082, demonstrating the intended directory shape.

- Establish one shared, explicit checkout discovery/path-resolution capability rather than fixing individual commands independently. Anchor the product default runtime root to the canonical Refine checkout, not process CWD, HOME, XDG_STATE_HOME, install mode, or service-manager mode.
- Route CLI lifecycle commands, installed-service generation and repair, daemon handoffs, deployed update/source promotion, web/Desktop lifecycle surfaces, and installer/runbook paths through the same invariant. Preserve port scoping and multi-checkout isolation.

Correct the production split-brain in Refine runtime and binary path ownership.

Desired invariant:
- A Refine checkout is the sole product home for its executable and runtime artifacts in every supported launch mode.
- Whether operators run ./r system start, ./r system install --port 8082 followed by service-manager lifecycle, the checkout-local deployed binary directly, or source-promotion/update flows, all normal production runtime files for a port resolve to the same canonical <refine-checkout>/run/<port> tree.
- The stable deployed binary remains <refine-checkout>/bin/refine and installed service definitions execute that checkout-local binary. Do not copy or relocate the Refine binary into ~/.local, XDG application-state directories, or another user-global install location.
- OS-required registration files may remain in their platform-required locations, such as the systemd user-unit or launchd plist directory, but they must reference the checkout-local binary, use the Refine checkout as the working directory, and pass the absolute checkout-local runtime root.

Observed evidence in current main:
- src/surfaces/cli/actions/system.rs defaults --runtime-root to the relative path run, and src/surfaces/cli/dispatch.rs resolves relative CLI paths from the current working directory. Direct binary use outside the checkout can therefore create or consult a second run tree.
- src/process/supervisor/runtime/mod.rs exposes RuntimeRoot::installed_user and RuntimePathLayout::for_os, which models Linux installed runtime state at ${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/refine/run and analogous non-checkout roots on other platforms.
- src/tools/host/installation/backend_spec.rs consumes that OS-specific layout for installed-service metadata, preserving the incorrect alternative product-home concept.
- scripts/install.sh and r already intend the deployed executable to be <checkout>/bin/refine; preserve and strengthen this behavior.
- The live development instance on port 8082 currently reports /home/buddy/projects/refine/run/8082, demonstrating the intended directory shape.

Implementation constraints:
- Establish one shared, explicit checkout discovery/path-resolution capability rather than fixing individual commands independently. Anchor the product default runtime root to the canonical Refine checkout, not process CWD, HOME, XDG_STATE_HOME, install mode, or service-manager mode.
- Route CLI lifecycle commands, installed-service generation and repair, daemon handoffs, deployed update/source promotion, web/Desktop lifecycle surfaces, and installer/runbook paths through the same invariant. Preserve port scoping and multi-checkout isolation.
- Remove or retire production use of RuntimeRoot::installed_user and OS-specific app-support runtime-root selection. Keep separately required credential stores and service-registration locations platform appropriate.
- Preserve explicit injectable runtime roots where test harnesses or deliberately isolated internal execution require them, but normal user-facing start/install/update/repair/status flows must not silently select an external or caller-CWD run directory.
- Detect legacy external runtime/install state safely. Do not silently merge, delete, or overwrite either tree. Provide clear diagnostics and an auditable, non-destructive migration or repair path if existing installed services point outside the checkout.
- Preserve confirmation boundaries for update, uninstall, source promotion, approval, and merge. Do not approve or merge this Goal.
- Update intent and specification, CLI reference, install and upgrade runbooks, and ontology statements that currently permit user-global runtime roots.

Verification:
- Add regression tests proving system start and system install for the same checkout and port resolve byte-for-byte to <checkout>/run/<port>, including invocation from a different CWD and direct use of <checkout>/bin/refine.
- Assert generated systemd, launchd, and service metadata uses the checkout-local binary, checkout working directory, and absolute checkout-local runtime root; assert no production path is ~/.local, XDG state, or another external app-support runtime.
- Cover install, repair, start, stop, restart, status, update, source-promotion handoff, and non-destructive legacy detection at focused shared boundaries.
- Run focused runtime, installation, daemon-lifecycle, CLI, deployed-update, and source-promotion tests; production binary install and install-uninstall coverage; cargo check --all-targets; cargo fmt --all -- --check; documentation contract tests; and git diff --check. Report any unrelated baseline failure or unavailable environment-dependent test separately.

findings.description: P5 simultaneously says an exact external bundle executable is recorded per checkout, conflicting ownership is rejected, and the same fabricated external bundle must launch successfully for two checkouts. Those are incompatible ownership models. P4 also accepts any canonical --refine-checkout value but does not require the external executable and anchor to match the durable launcher registration, so a mistaken or arbitrary caller can select another valid checkout.
findings.recommendation: Choose and document one authority model. If a shared external bundle is intentionally parameterized per invocation, make the checkout-owned, port-scoped launcher record the durable authority and do not call the shared bundle path a conflicting owner; validate the launcher record, executable path, checkout identity, and invocation nonce or equivalent correlation together. If bundles are checkout-owned one-to-one, reject the same-bundle/two-checkout case and provision distinct bundle identities. Add tampered-but-otherwise-valid checkout-anchor tests.

findings.description: The proposed external launch anchor contains only --refine-checkout, while the retained Desktop chooses its port independently from REFINE_DESKTOP_PORT or a default. The removed Desktop bridge also wrote desktop-state.json and desktop-events.jsonl directly under the supplied runtime root, not under run/<port>. Thus checkout ownership alone does not guarantee the requested checkout-and-port ownership or prevent a launcher for one installation from connecting to or writing state for another port.
findings.recommendation: Make the resolved Desktop launch identity a single validated value containing canonical checkout plus authoritative port, derive both run and run/<port> from it, and pass the port through the checkout-owned launcher rather than a free environment default. Move Desktop state/events and other port-specific artifacts under the resolved port root. Test non-8082 ports, two ports in one checkout, actual state writes, daemon URL selection, and checkout/port disagreement failures.

findings.description: P4 preserves REFINE_RUNTIME_ROOT by accepting any absolute value before checkout resolution, but calling it test/internal does not enforce that boundary. In a production Desktop binary this remains an unrestricted bypass of the owning-checkout anchor and can silently select an external runtime tree; precedence against --refine-checkout is also unspecified.
findings.recommendation: Make isolated runtime injection a test-only constructor or compile-time/internal capability that normal packaged entrypoints cannot exercise. If an environment escape hatch must ship, require an explicit internal mode, reject it for packaged launches, define mutual exclusion with checkout anchors, and test production entrypoints with absolute, relative, and conflicting override values.

findings.description: P3 requires systemd/launchd/Windows service metadata to execute <checkout>/bin/refine for the daemon, while P5 says OS shortcut/Login Item metadata must invoke the Desktop launcher. The current macOS installation model uses one launchd_login_item registration for daemon startup. The plan does not distinguish daemon service registration from Desktop application launch registration, so implementing P5 by repurposing that plist would break P3 and lifecycle control.
findings.recommendation: Define separate registration artifacts, labels, schemas, and owners for daemon lifecycle and Desktop launch. Specify install, update, rollback, repair, and uninstall behavior for each, including partial failure and stale-registration recovery, and verify both can coexist for the same checkout/port without either overwriting or controlling the other.

findings.description: The retained Round 2 Windows service manifest passes --runtime-root but omits --port even when installation state is port-scoped. P3's metadata assertions mention executable, working directory, and runtime root but do not explicitly require the selected port in every platform format. Replaying this code can start the default port while recording installation state under another port.
findings.recommendation: Require every generated systemd, launchd, and Windows service definition to carry the exact selected non-default port as well as binary, working directory, and runtime root. Add a Windows regression with a non-8082 port and assert status/control/repair parse the same port back from metadata.

Desired invariant:

Observed evidence in current main:
- src/surfaces/cli/actions/system.rs defaults --runtime-root to the relative path run, and src/surfaces/cli/dispatch.rs resolves relative CLI paths from the current working directory. Direct binary use outside the checkout can therefore create or consult a second run tree.

findings.description: P5 simultaneously says an exact external bundle executable is recorded per checkout, conflicting ownership is rejected, and the same fabricated external bundle must launch successfully for two checkouts. Those are incompatible ownership models. P4 also accepts any canonical --refine-checkout value but does not require the external executable and anchor to match the durable launcher registration, so a mistaken or arbitrary caller can select another valid checkout.
findings.recommendation: Choose and document one authority model. If a shared external bundle is intentionally parameterized per invocation, make the checkout-owned, port-scoped launcher record the durable authority and do not call the shared bundle path a conflicting owner; validate the launcher record, executable path, checkout identity, and invocation nonce or equivalent correlation together. If bundles are checkout-owned one-to-one, reject the same-bundle/two-checkout case and provision distinct bundle identities. Add tampered-but-otherwise-valid checkout-anchor tests.

findings.description: The proposed external launch anchor contains only --refine-checkout, while the retained Desktop chooses its port independently from REFINE_DESKTOP_PORT or a default. The removed Desktop bridge also wrote desktop-state.json and desktop-events.jsonl directly under the supplied runtime root, not under run/<port>. Thus checkout ownership alone does not guarantee the requested checkout-and-port ownership or prevent a launcher for one installation from connecting to or writing state for another port.
findings.recommendation: Make the resolved Desktop launch identity a single validated value containing canonical checkout plus authoritative port, derive both run and run/<port> from it, and pass the port through the checkout-owned launcher rather than a free environment default. Move Desktop state/events and other port-specific artifacts under the resolved port root. Test non-8082 ports, two ports in one checkout, actual state writes, daemon URL selection, and checkout/port disagreement failures.

findings.description: P4 preserves REFINE_RUNTIME_ROOT by accepting any absolute value before checkout resolution, but calling it test/internal does not enforce that boundary. findings.recommendation: Make isolated runtime injection a test-only constructor or compile-time/internal capability that normal packaged entrypoints cannot exercise. If an environment escape hatch must ship, require an explicit internal mode, reject it for packaged launches, define mutual exclusion with checkout anchors, and test production entrypoints with absolute, relative, and conflicting override values.

findings.description: P3 requires systemd/launchd/Windows service metadata to execute <checkout>/bin/refine for the daemon, while P5 says OS shortcut/Login Item metadata must invoke the Desktop launcher. The current macOS installation model uses one launchd_login_item registration for daemon startup. The plan does not distinguish daemon service registration from Desktop application launch registration, so implementing P5 by repurposing that plist would break P3 and lifecycle control.
findings.recommendation: Define separate registration artifacts, labels, schemas, and owners for daemon lifecycle and Desktop launch. Specify install, update, rollback, repair, and uninstall behavior for each, including partial failure and stale-registration recovery, and verify both can coexist for the same checkout/port without either overwriting or controlling the other.

findings.description: The retained Round 2 Windows service manifest passes --runtime-root but omits --port even when installation state is port-scoped. P3's metadata assertions mention executable, working directory, and runtime root but do not explicitly require the selected port in every platform format. Replaying this code can start the default port while recording installation state under another port.
findings.recommendation: Require every generated systemd, launchd, and Windows service definition to carry the exact selected non-default port as well as binary, working directory, and runtime root. Add a Windows regression with a non-8082 port and assert status/control/repair parse the same port back from metadata.

findings.description: The retained shared checkout capability identifies a checkout partly by scripts/install.sh, but current main deliberately removed that file in commit 00d8e0d1 and now uses docs/runbooks/install.md in checkout detection. The proposed tests do not explicitly assert discovery of this real linked worktree using current-main markers.
